Docket EL25-49 — Constellation Energy limited protest
Constellation protests aspects of PJM's co-location compliance filing
The most live item across all eight FERC dockets. A major generation owner is contesting the compliance terms, so PJM's August filing must not be treated as settled rules.
Case PUR-2025-00058 — order granting motion to adjust the GS-5 compliance filing for six customers electing to remain on GS-4
The Commission reopened the 2025 biennial review and let Dominion adjust its GS-5 compliance filing to reflect six customers electing under 2026 Va. Acts ch. 1124 to stay on Rate Schedule GS-4

The live implementation vehicle for GS-5. The November 2025 final order created the class effective 1 January 2027; 2026 opt-out legislation then let certain customers remain on GS-4, and six did. Revenues and billing determinants move accordingly with offsetting adjustments to final GS-4 and GS-5 rates. Anyone modelling GS-5 rates should wait for the compliance filing rather than rely on the November 2025 apportionment.
Dominion compliance filing of revised GS-5 tariffs, due at least 45 days before 1 January 2027

Case PUR-2026-00114 — order for notice and hearing on NOVEC revisions to the terms and conditions of Rate Schedules LP-1, DPS, HV-1 and HV-2
The SCC docketed NOVEC's petition revising the terms and conditions of its four large-load tariffs and let the revisions take effect on an interim basis from 1 September 2026

NOVEC serves a large share of Loudoun and Prince William data-centre load, and its Large Power Service, Delivery Point Service and two dedicated-facilities schedules are already live in revised form. NOVEC says the revisions insulate other members from large-load costs and proposes no rate change, but the terms are provisional and can be modified at hearing. This case number was previously recorded as non-existent and mis-attributed to Dominion.

Incremental to the base generation plan. Weather-normalised retail sales growth reached 9.6%, a tenth consecutive quarter at or above guidance, with committed load still flat at 4.5 GW.
PJM Cycle 1 interconnection queue results under the reformed process
715 projects totalling 201.5 GW qualify for Cycle 1; no backlog remains from prior queues

Queue reform is operational and the historic backlog is cleared, so new generation to serve large load now sits on a defined study track rather than an open-ended queue. PJM expects demand up to 70 GW higher by 2038, largely data centres, against 51 GW already under signed interconnection agreements.
Ameren Missouri rate case claims ~$11M of annual base-rate savings from committed data centre customers
Quantified ratepayer benefit before the first MW is served — $21M projected over two years. A useful counterweight to cost-shift arguments appearing in other jurisdictions.
Ameren reports 2.8 GW of executed ESAs plus 0.6 GW of construction agreements without an ESA

The 0.6 GW distinction matters — construction agreements without an ESA are a weaker commitment than a signed ESA and should not be counted alongside them. A further 4 GW of proposed projects have completed interconnection studies. Google and Amazon broke ground in Montgomery County with $25bn combined planned investment.
Case PUR-2026-00056 — final order approving the Rider T1 transmission rate adjustment clause on an amended 12-CP allocation
The Commission approved Rider T1 effective 1 September 2026 on an amended 12-CP methodology that folds the GS-5 minimum demand charge into the transmission allocation factor

This is where Virginia actually moved transmission cost responsibility onto large load. The minimum-demand adjustment cuts the residential allocation factor by 2.84% and raises GS-4 by 4.33%, taking the typical residential increase from $2.90 to $0.94 a month. The Commission declined broad direct assignment of supplemental-project costs for now, instead ordering a new docket on amending Dominion's line extension policy.
Final order entered; tariff sheets acknowledged 2026-08-12
Dominion to file an amended line extension policy within 90 days and a cross-EDC cost assignment update within 120 days
Dominion contracted capacity ladder: SELOA 32.4 GW, CLOA 9.4 GW, ESA 12.0 GW as of July 2026

The only published stage-by-stage conversion ladder in the coverage set, with a series back to July 2023. CLOA FELL from 11.0 GW in December to 9.4 GW while ESA rose from 10.2 to 12.0 — direct evidence of conversion rather than pipeline growth.
Xcel recommends ~2,600 MW of company-owned generation at SPS, ~70% of the selected RFP portfolio

Self-build rather than PPA procurement changes the counterparty question for anyone siting in the Panhandle. SPS base capex is $19.0B for 2026-2030. Minnesota's 100 MW large-load tariff was approved this quarter; Colorado and Wisconsin are filed.
